claims.claim_ar: توظيف لفظة «اللقاء» مجازاً للدلالة على القتال، أي استعمال لقاء (القيام بالالتقاء) للاشارة إلى المعركة والقتال.
claims.claim_en: The term “al-liqaaʾ” (meeting) is used metaphorically to mean fighting — using 'meeting' to denote battle/encounter in combat.

claims.claim_ar: الاقتصار والاختصار بعدم وصف طائفة الكفار وتقديم الإشارة المجملة بدلاً من التفصيل، دلالة على الإيجاز والاختصار البلاغي.
claims.claim_en: The omission of any detailed description of the enemy-group ("and he omitted describing it") is a rhetorical brevity/conciseness (hasr/qasr), using omission instead of detailed depiction.
claims.needs_review_reason: Assigned root/lemma from the referenced group (الكفار) because the comment refers to omission about that group; verify attachment and whether another root would be preferable.

claims.source_quote_ar: وفيه إشعار بأنّ على العبد أن لا يفتر عن ذكر ربه
claims.claim_ar: الآية/الخطاب فيها إشارة إلى وجوب الاستمرار في ذكر الله وعدم الانقطاع عنه — قراءة بلاغية تعتبرها أمراً ونصيحة (إيجاب/إنشاء).
claims.claim_en: The commentary reads the passage as implying an injunction: the servant must not desist from remembering God — a rhetorical effect of exhortation/command (ijab/inshaa).
claims.needs_review_reason: The commentary's exhortatory reading is generalized; confirm that this injunction is being derived from this specific verse rather than nearby verses or homiletic expansion.

warnings: Provided source chunks are from Zamakhshari and Safi (al-Kashshaf, al-Jadwal etc.). The developer instruction requested extracts from al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, and tafsir_balagha sections; those specific authors/sections were not present in the supplied chunks.

Some claims are mapped to ayah-level (word_index 0) because the commentary speaks about the style or moral implication of the verse rather than a single lexical item; verify intended word assignment if a different anchoring is preferred.
